answer: A robot network resists Sybil attacks through optical distance-bounding at a harbor jetty. Nodes authenticate by firing violet laser pulses at retroreflectors near shoreline juniper stands to verify distinct physical coordinates via time-of-flight ranging. An attacker incurs heavy capital costs deploying discrete transceivers at physical locations rather than spawning virtual instances. However, dense sea fog scatters optical beams, occasionally causing false rejections of honest nodes.
